books.title: Superintelligence
books.subtitle: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
books.pitch: The book that turned the AI control problem into a serious field: if we build minds smarter than us, our future depends on getting their goals right the first time.

books.title: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
books.subtitle: Why Superhuman AI Would Kill Us All
books.pitch: The bluntest case yet from MIRI: superhuman AI grown with today's methods would want things we did not intend, and it would win. So the world should stop building it.

books.title: AI: Unexplainable, Unpredictable, Uncontrollable
books.pitch: A computer scientist argues there may be hard limits: advanced AI cannot be fully explained, predicted or controlled, so we should be far more careful about building it.

books.title: Human Compatible
books.subtitle: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Control
books.pitch: The co-author of the main AI textbook says the standard way of building AI, giving machines fixed goals, is broken, and proposes machines that are humble about what we want.

books.title: Life 3.0
books.subtitle: Being Human in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
books.pitch: An MIT physicist opens with a thriller about a team that builds a superintelligence, then maps the futures it could lead to, from utopia to extinction, and asks which one we want.

books.title: The Alignment Problem
books.subtitle: Machine Learning and Human Values
books.pitch: A beautifully told history of how machine learning systems learn the wrong lessons, from biased predictions to reward hacking, and the researchers trying to fix it.

books.title: The Precipice
books.subtitle: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity
books.pitch: An Oxford philosopher puts numbers on the risks that could end humanity's future. His biggest single risk for the next century: unaligned AI.

books.title: The Coming Wave
books.subtitle: Technology, Power, and the Twenty-first Century's Greatest Dilemma
books.pitch: A DeepMind co-founder, now running Microsoft AI, argues that AI and synthetic biology will spread like every technology before them, and that we must find a way to contain them anyway.

books.title: Our Final Invention
books.subtitle: Artificial Intelligence and the End of the Human Era
books.pitch: A documentary filmmaker interviews the people who saw it coming, years before ChatGPT, and argues an intelligence explosion could end the human era.

books.title: The Singularity Is Near
books.subtitle: When Humans Transcend Biology
books.pitch: The optimist's bible: technology grows exponentially, human level AI arrives around 2029 and a singularity merges humans and machines by 2045.

books.title: The Singularity Is Nearer
books.subtitle: When We Merge with AI
books.pitch: Nearly twenty years later, Kurzweil checks his forecasts against large language models and doubles down: 2029 for human level AI, 2045 for the singularity.

books.title: Deep Utopia
books.subtitle: Life and Meaning in a Solved World
books.pitch: Superintelligence was about what could go wrong. This is about what happens if it goes right: when machines can do everything, what is left for us to do and why?

books.title: Rationality: From AI to Zombies
books.pitch: The Sequences: 333 essays on thinking clearly, changing your mind and why building AI with the right values is so hard. The book that grew the rationalist and AI safety communities.

books.title: Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society
books.pitch: The Center for AI Safety's free textbook: catastrophic risks, how AI works, safety engineering, complex systems, ethics, collective action and governance in one place.

books.title: Uncontrollable
books.subtitle: The Threat of Artificial Superintelligence and the Race to Save the World
books.pitch: Written for people with no technical background, it explains what AI is, why superintelligence could slip out of control, and what ordinary citizens can do.

books.title: The Age of AI
books.subtitle: And Our Human Future
books.pitch: A statesman, a former Google CEO and an MIT dean ask what AI means for knowledge, security, world order and what it is to be human.

books.title: Genius Makers
books.subtitle: The Mavericks Who Brought AI to Google, Facebook, and the World
books.pitch: A New York Times reporter tells the story of deep learning's rise: the outsiders, the bidding wars, and the safety fears that came with success.

books.title: Empire of AI
books.subtitle: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI
books.pitch: An investigative reporter argues OpenAI became an empire: taking data, labour and resources from around the world in the name of AGI.

books.title: The Optimist
books.subtitle: Sam Altman, OpenAI, and the Race to Invent the Future
books.pitch: A Wall Street Journal reporter's biography of Sam Altman, from childhood in St. Louis to the boardroom crisis of 2023.

books.title: Supremacy
books.subtitle: AI, ChatGPT, and the Race That Will Change the World
books.pitch: The story of Demis Hassabis and Sam Altman, two idealists who set out to build safe AGI and ended up tied to big tech.

books.title: AI Snake Oil
books.subtitle: What Artificial Intelligence Can Do, What It Can't, and How to Tell the Difference
books.pitch: Two Princeton computer scientists separate real AI progress from hype, and argue advanced AI is not an existential threat. The best skeptical counterweight on this shelf.

books.title: What We Owe the Future
books.pitch: The case for longtermism: future people count, there could be a huge number of them, and we can shape their world, including by getting AI right.

books.title: The Technological Singularity
books.pitch: A short, calm guide from a DeepMind and Imperial College researcher to how we might get to superintelligence and what it would mean.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence
books.subtitle: A Guide for Thinking Humans
books.pitch: A complexity scientist explains how AI really works and argues that machines still lack understanding, the 'barrier of meaning'.

books.title: Rebooting AI
books.subtitle: Building Artificial Intelligence We Can Trust
books.pitch: Two scientists argue deep learning alone will not give us AI we can trust, and that we need common sense, reasoning and knowledge.

books.title: Army of None
books.subtitle: Autonomous Weapons and the Future of War
books.pitch: A former Army Ranger who helped write Pentagon policy on autonomy explains how machines are learning to kill, and how we could keep humans in charge.

books.title: Brief Answers to the Big Questions
books.pitch: Hawking's last book answers ten big questions, from God to black holes. One whole chapter asks whether AI will outsmart us, and warns it could be the best or worst thing to happen to humanity.

books.title: Smarter Than Us
books.subtitle: The Rise of Machine Intelligence
books.pitch: A short, sharp introduction by an Oxford researcher: why telling a superintelligence what we want is much harder than it sounds.

books.title: Artificial Superintelligence
books.subtitle: A Futuristic Approach
books.pitch: An early technical book on superintelligence safety, including a whole chapter on the limits of recursively self-improving AI and how to confine an AI in a box.

books.title: Situational Awareness
books.subtitle: The Decade Ahead
books.pitch: A former OpenAI researcher's book length essay series: count the orders of magnitude, expect AGI around 2027, then an intelligence explosion to superintelligence.

books.title: The Coming Technological Singularity
books.subtitle: How to Survive in the Post-Human Era
books.publisher: VISION-21 Symposium, NASA Lewis Research Center (NASA CP-10129)
books.pitch: The essay that made 'the Singularity' famous: within thirty years we will be able to create superhuman intelligence, and shortly after the human era will end.

books.title: Darwin among the Machines
books.subtitle: A letter to the editor
books.pitch: Four years after Darwin's Origin of Species, a young sheep farmer in New Zealand asks whether machines might evolve and one day rule us. The oldest warning on this shelf.

books.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
books.publisher: Mind, vol. 59, no. 236, Oxford University Press
books.pitch: The paper that asked 'Can machines think?' and proposed the imitation game, now called the Turing test. It ends with a plan for learning machines.

books.title: Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine
books.publisher: Advances in Computers, vol. 6, Academic Press
books.pitch: The source of the phrase 'intelligence explosion'. Good argues an ultraintelligent machine could design better machines, and would be the last invention we need, if it stays docile.

books.title: Intelligence Explosion Microeconomics
books.subtitle: MIRI technical report 2013-1
books.pitch: Yudkowsky's long attempt to turn the intelligence explosion into an empirical question: what are the returns when a mind reinvests in making itself smarter?

books.title: AI 2027
books.subtitle: A scenario
books.pitch: A month by month story of AI from mid 2025: coding automation, self-improving AI, a superhuman AI researcher, and two endings, a race and a slowdown.

books.title: The Age of Em
books.subtitle: Work, Love, and Life when Robots Rule the Earth
books.pitch: An economist takes one path to advanced AI, copying human brains into software, and works out in detail what the world of those copies might look like.

books.title: Rise of the Robots
books.subtitle: Technology and the Threat of a Jobless Future
books.pitch: A software entrepreneur argues that this time automation is different: machines are starting to do mental work, and many jobs may not come back.

books.title: The Master Algorithm
books.subtitle: How the Quest for the Ultimate Learning Machine Will Remake Our World
books.pitch: A tour of the five schools of machine learning and a bet that one universal learning algorithm could one day learn anything from data.

books.title: Atlas of AI
books.subtitle: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
books.pitch: AI is not weightless or magic. Crawford follows it to the mines, warehouses, datasets and state agencies it depends on, and asks who it serves.

books.title: Weapons of Math Destruction
books.subtitle: How Big Data Increases Inequality and Threatens Democracy
books.pitch: A mathematician who worked in finance shows how opaque scoring models punish the poor, and how they spread from schools to jobs, loans and courts.

books.title: AI Superpowers
books.subtitle: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order
books.pitch: A veteran of Apple, Microsoft and Google China argues that AI is now about execution and data, which favours China, and that the real crisis will be jobs.

books.title: Prediction Machines
books.subtitle: The Simple Economics of Artificial Intelligence
books.pitch: Three economists boil AI down to one thing: it makes prediction cheap. Then they show what that does to decisions, jobs and strategy.

books.title: The Human Use of Human Beings
books.subtitle: Cybernetics and Society
books.pitch: The founder of cybernetics explains feedback and communication for a general reader, and warns early that automatic machines could harm workers and society.

books.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines
books.subtitle: When Computers Exceed Human Intelligence
books.pitch: Kurzweil's early case that computing power grows exponentially and that machines will match human intelligence around 2029, with dated predictions you can check.

books.title: Surviving AI
books.subtitle: The Promise and Peril of Artificial Intelligence
books.pitch: A short, clear walk from today's narrow AI to general AI and superintelligence, and why making it friendly is the key problem of the century.

books.title: Nexus
books.subtitle: A Brief History of Information Networks from the Stone Age to AI
books.pitch: The historian behind Sapiens argues that information is about connection more than truth, and that AI is the first technology that can make decisions and create ideas by itself.

books.title: Homo Deus
books.subtitle: A Brief History of Tomorrow
books.pitch: Having beaten much of famine, plague and war, humans may aim for immortality, happiness and godlike powers, while algorithms come to know us better than we know ourselves.

books.title: Computer Power and Human Reason
books.subtitle: From Judgment to Calculation
books.pitch: The creator of the ELIZA chatbot was shocked that people confided in it. Here he argues there are tasks computers should never be given, whether or not they can do them.

books.title: What Computers Still Can't Do
books.subtitle: A Critique of Artificial Reason
books.pitch: A philosopher's famous attack on early AI: human intelligence rests on bodies, skills and context that rule based programs cannot capture.

books.title: The Myth of Artificial Intelligence
books.subtitle: Why Computers Can't Think the Way We Do
books.publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
books.pitch: A computer scientist argues that today's AI cannot do abduction, the everyday leap to the best explanation, and that hype about general AI is a myth that hurts science.

books.title: Power and Progress
books.subtitle: Our Thousand-Year Struggle over Technology and Prosperity
books.pitch: Two economists, later Nobel laureates, show that new technology only helps most people when power is shared, and argue AI is heading the wrong way.

books.title: Co-Intelligence
books.subtitle: Living and Working with AI
books.pitch: A Wharton professor's practical guide to working with today's AI as a strange new kind of colleague, with simple rules for using it well.

books.title: Unmasking AI
books.subtitle: My Mission to Protect What Is Human in a World of Machines
books.pitch: A computer scientist found face recognition could not see her dark skinned face until she wore a white mask. Her memoir follows the research and activism that followed.

books.title: Four Battlegrounds
books.subtitle: Power in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
books.pitch: The author of Army of None maps the global contest over AI power across four battlegrounds: data, computing power, talent and institutions.

books.title: Global Catastrophic Risks
books.pitch: An early scholarly survey of risks that could cripple human civilisation, from asteroids and pandemics to nuclear war, nanotechnology and AI.

books.title: Possible Minds
books.subtitle: Twenty-Five Ways of Looking at AI
books.pitch: Brockman asked twenty five scientists and thinkers to respond to Norbert Wiener's 1950 warnings about machines. The answers range from deep worry to calm optimism.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.pitch: The standard textbook of the deep learning era, from the maths you need to the research frontier of 2016. The authors keep a free online version.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.subtitle: Fourth Edition
books.pitch: The most used AI textbook in the world. The fourth edition adds deep learning and ends with chapters on ethics, safety and the future of AI.

books.title: Dive into Deep Learning
books.pitch: An open source, hands on textbook where every idea comes with runnable code. Used in hundreds of universities and free online.

books.title: Frankenstein
books.subtitle: or, The Modern Prometheus
books.publisher: Lackington, Hughes, Harding, Mavor and Jones (London)
books.pitch: The first great story about making a mind. A young scientist creates a living being, abandons it, and learns that creators owe something to what they create.

books.title: Erewhon
books.subtitle: or, Over the Range
books.pitch: A satirical utopia where people smashed their machines centuries ago, because a philosopher warned that machines were evolving towards consciousness faster than humans.

books.title: The Machine Stops
books.pitch: Written in 1909, a short story about people living alone underground, served by a global Machine that meets every need, until it starts to fail.

books.title: R.U.R.
books.subtitle: Rossum's Universal Robots
books.publisher: English version by Paul Selver and Nigel Playfair, Doubleday, Page (1923)
books.pitch: The 1920 play that gave the world the word robot. A factory makes artificial workers, the world comes to depend on them, and the robots rise up.

books.title: I, Robot
books.pitch: Nine linked stories about robots built with the Three Laws of Robotics, and all the ways simple rules go strange in practice.

books.title: Accelerando
books.pitch: A family saga across three generations that runs straight through the technological singularity, from dot com hustlers to minds spread across the solar system.

books.title: Klara and the Sun
books.pitch: A Nobel laureate's quiet novel told by Klara, an Artificial Friend bought to keep a sick girl company, who watches people with love and misunderstanding.

books.title: The Lifecycle of Software Objects
books.pitch: A novella about digital creatures raised like children over many years, and the people who refuse to give up on them when the market moves on.

books.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
books.pitch: A bounty hunter retires escaped androids in a ruined San Francisco, and starts to doubt what separates them from humans. The basis for Blade Runner.

books.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
books.pitch: The paper that turned vague AI safety worries into five concrete research problems that engineers could work on with today's machine learning.

books.title: Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems
books.pitch: Training can produce a model that is itself an optimiser with its own goal. This paper names that mesa-optimiser and the inner alignment problem.

books.title: Is Power-Seeking AI an Existential Risk?
books.pitch: A careful report that breaks the AI risk argument into six claims, gives each a probability, and ends with a rough estimate of the chance of catastrophe by 2070.

books.title: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks
books.pitch: A clear map of how AI could lead to catastrophe, sorted into four sources: malicious use, racing, organisational failures and rogue AIs.

books.title: The Basic AI Drives
books.publisher: Proceedings of the First AGI Conference (IOS Press)
books.pitch: A short paper that argues almost any goal seeking AI will develop the same drives: to improve itself, protect itself, keep its goals and gain resources.

books.title: Machines of Loving Grace
books.subtitle: How AI Could Transform the World for the Better
books.pitch: Anthropic's CEO sketches what could go right if powerful AI arrives and goes well: a compressed century of progress in biology, the mind, the economy and governance.

books.title: AI as Normal Technology
books.subtitle: An alternative to the vision of AI as a potential superintelligence
books.publisher: Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University
books.pitch: The authors of AI Snake Oil argue AI will be transformative but normal, like electricity: adoption takes decades, and humans stay in control through ordinary institutions.

books.title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress
books.pitch: Twenty five leading scientists, including three Turing Award winners, warn that AI may soon outpace our ability to control it, and set out what research and governance must do now.

books.title: International AI Safety Report
books.publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology; arXiv:2501.17805
books.pitch: The first global scientific review of what general-purpose AI can do, what could go wrong, and how risks can be managed, guided by an expert panel nominated by more than 30 countries and international organisations.

books.title: The Bletchley Declaration
books.subtitle: by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023
books.pitch: The first statement signed by the US, China, the EU and 26 others that frontier AI could cause serious, even catastrophic, harm and that the risks need international cooperation.

authors.name: Governments at the AI Safety Summit
